title: Kernel-based potential mean-field games with unbiased random Fourier $U$-statistics
abstract: arXiv:2605.29371v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study the subclass of potential mean-field games in which the running interaction cost and the terminal target cost are both expressed through reproducing-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) penalties, and develop a computational framework that exploits this kernel structure. Both costs are estimated from finite-sample empirical distributions using a random Fourier U-statistic representation that is unbiased and has linear cost in the batch size. The drift of the controlled diffusion is parametrized by a neural network and trained via stochastic gradient descent. For population near-minimizers we prove convergence to the terminal-constrained problem as the penalty diverges, and show that the same limit is recovered almost surely when the learned controls are evaluated on independent finite samples under explicit coupling conditions on the penalty, random-feature count and sample size. tldr: 本文针对运行成本与终端成本均由核MMD惩罚刻画的势均场博弈，提出了一种基于无偏随机傅里叶U统计量的计算框架，以神经网络参数化漂移并通过随机梯度下降训练，同时证明了在惩罚发散及显式耦合条件下向终端约束问题的收敛性。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a computational framework for potential mean-field games with kernel-MMD-based running and terminal costs, using unbiased random Fourier U-statistics for cost estimation and neural-network-parametrized drifts, with proven convergence to the terminal-constrained problem under explicit coupling conditions.
